problem: Users need to export saved Cubik animations to portable files for sharing (peer-to-peer, archival, version control), and import animation files back into their device's animation library. The exchange format must be compact (typical LED-matrix animations are sparse), human-readable for manual inspection/editing, and self-describing (matrix dimensions, name, frames). Imports must validate untrusted input — reject malformed, oversized, or off-spec files without corrupting the local library. Round-trip must preserve animation fidelity exactly: export-then-import yields the same animation. Sharing channels: file download/upload and clipboard JSON paste.

versions.note: Naive architecture: frontend↔backend with single codec module, sparse JSON wire format, file + clipboard channels; no validator yet (R-validate-import unsatisfied by design)
Hardened v1: validator gating import path, versioned format_sparse, conflict resolution mode (default rename-with-suffix); Concern ontology added (data_integrity, portability, usability, performance)

stressors.description: Adversarial or accidentally malformed import payload: not JSON, missing required fields, wrong types, color/coord values out of range, or oversized payload (10s of MB) intended to exhaust memory or storage
stressors.attractor: System gets pushed toward strict boundary validation: hard size cap on payload, schema validation against format_sparse contract before any persistence work, value-range checks on coords/colors, transactional commit only after all checks pass
stressors.solution: Add an input-validation layer at import_endpoint that rejects oversized payloads, schema-violating JSON, and out-of-range pixel/color values before any persistence. Pair with an actionable error contract.

stressors.description: User imports an animation whose name already exists in the saved library; without policy the second insert either fails opaquely, silently overwrites, or creates duplicates
stressors.attractor: System gets pushed toward explicit conflict-resolution policy at import time: detect collision before commit, give user a rename/overwrite/cancel choice, default to rename-with-suffix to never destroy data silently
stressors.solution: Detect existing-name collision in import_endpoint before commit; expose a resolution mode (rename|overwrite|cancel) on the API; default to rename-with-suffix so existing animations are never silently overwritten.

stressors.description: Format must evolve over time (new fields, semantic changes). Old clients receive new-format files, new clients receive old-format files; without versioning these mix silently and round-trip stops being faithful
stressors.attractor: System gets pushed toward an explicit format version field with semver-style compatibility rules: codec rejects unknown major versions with clear error, ignores unknown minor-version fields (additive evolution), exporter writes the version it produced
stressors.solution: Introduce explicit "version" field in format_sparse following semver rules. Codec rejects unknown major version; tolerates unknown fields within a known major; exporter stamps the version it produced.
